fields.title: Squint
fields.bodyHtml:
Squint (strabismus) is a condition in which the eyes do not look in the same direction at the same time. It may be constant or intermittent and may show itself as the eye turning inwards (esotropia), outwards (exotropia), upwards (hypertropia) or downwards (hypotropia). Squint can occur in children and adults and causes not only a cosmetic concern but also problems with sight.

Diagnosis of squint

  1. Visual examination: the ophthalmologist carries out an initial examination of the eyes, assessing their position and their ability to fix on a point.
  2. Visual acuity tests: testing the sight of each eye separately to establish whether there is amblyopia (lazy eye) or other visual problems.
  3. Coordination tests: used to assess how well the eyes move together and to measure the angle of the squint.
  4. Refraction tests: measurement of refractive errors (short-sightedness, long-sightedness or astigmatism) using special lenses.
  5. Fundoscopy: examination of the inner structures of the eye to rule out other conditions that may affect sight and the position of the eyes.
  6. Gonioscopy and biomicroscopy: used for detailed examination of the angle of the anterior chamber and the state of the eye muscles.

Methods of treating squint

  1. Correction of vision:
    • Glasses or contact lenses: used to correct refractive errors that may be causing the squint.
    • Prism lenses: help shift the image to correct double vision and improve coordination of eye movement.
  2. Orthoptic exercises:
    • Specific exercises for the eye muscles that help improve the coordination and strength of the muscles responsible for eye movement.
    • Exercises may involve a synoptophore and other devices for training the visual system.
  3. Occlusion therapy:
    • The use of eye patches or special filters to cover the stronger eye temporarily and stimulate the work and development of the weaker one.
    • This method is effective in treating amblyopia, which often accompanies squint.
  4. Botulinum toxin injections:
    • Injection of botulinum toxin into the eye muscles to weaken their action temporarily, which can help correct the position of the eye.
    • The procedure is carried out under local anaesthetic and requires no lengthy recovery.
  5. Surgical treatment:
    • Muscle recession: weakening the action of strong muscles by moving their points of attachment.
    • Muscle resection: strengthening the action of weak muscles by shortening them.
    • Adjustable suture surgery: allows the surgeon to adjust the tension of the muscles during the operation to achieve the best result.

Advantages of treating squint in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: Israeli ophthalmologists have rich experience in treating squint in children and adults and use the most modern methods and technologies.
  2. An individual approach: every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of all aspects of their health and the state of their eyes.
  3. Modern equipment: clinics are equipped with the newest diagnostic and treatment devices, which ensures accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  4. A comprehensive approach: treatment covers not only surgery but also rehabilitation programmes, orthoptic exercises and psychological support for patients.
  5. A short recovery period: thanks to minimally invasive techniques and advanced technology, recovery after treatment is quick and causes the patient minimal discomfort.
  6. High standards of safety: Israeli clinics adhere strictly to international protocols and standards of medical care, which ensures safety and high quality.

Treatment of squint in Israel gives patients access to highly qualified medical care and improves both their sight and their quality of life.

fields.title: Lagophthalmos
fields.bodyHtml:
Lagophthalmos is a condition in which the eyelids cannot close completely, which leads to dryness and irritation of the eye. It can cause a number of complications, including infection and damage to the cornea. Lagophthalmos often arises from paralysis of the facial nerve, injury or complications after surgery.

Diagnosis of lagophthalmos

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor talks with the patient, gathering information about symptoms, previous illnesses, treatment and other factors that may affect the condition.
  2. Visual examination:
    • The ophthalmologist examines the patient's eyes and assesses the state of the eyelids, cornea and conjunctiva.
  3. Schirmer's test:
    • Measurement of the amount of tear fluid produced by the eye, to assess the degree of dryness.
  4. Ophthalmoscopy:
    • Assessment of the cornea and the fundus to identify any damage or changes.
  5. Fluorescein test:
    • The use of fluorescein dye to reveal damage to the cornea.
  6. Tonometry:
    • Measurement of the pressure inside the eye to rule out glaucoma and other associated conditions.

Treatment of lagophthalmos

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Artificial tears: drops to moisten the eyes and prevent dryness.
    • Eye ointments: soothing ointments used at night to protect the cornea.
    • Occlusion therapy: taping or special dressings over the eyelids to prevent tear fluid evaporating.
  2. Physiotherapy:
    • Eyelid massage: helps improve the blood supply and stimulate the eyelid muscles.
    • Warm compresses: help relax the muscles and improve tear production.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Tarsorrhaphy: partial or complete joining of the eyelids to narrow the opening of the eye and protect the cornea.
    • Implantation of a gold or platinum weight in the upper eyelid: a small weight is fitted that helps the eyelid close under gravity.
    • Myectomy and myoplasty: surgical procedures that alter the eyelid muscles to improve their function and allow the eye to close.
  4. Treatment of the underlying condition:
    • Where lagophthalmos is caused by facial nerve paralysis, the underlying condition must be treated, which may involve medication or surgery.

Advantages of treating lagophthalmos in Israel

  1. A high level of medical expertise:
    • Israel has leading specialists in ophthalmology with many years of experience and exceptional skills.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and materials, including tarsorrhaphy and eyelid weight implantation.
  5. Comfortable conditions:
    • Patients can count on a high level of comfort and service during treatment and recovery.

Treatment of lagophthalmos in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves their quality of life.

fields.title: Treatment of back pain
fields.bodyHtml:
The orthopaedics department of the leading private clinic Assuta provides consultations for patients suffering from back pain. Thanks to the high qualifications of its specialists and its modern equipment, the clinic attracts patients from around the world, helping them deal successfully with a range of conditions and regain the pleasure of movement and their ability to work.

Back pain is often caused by degenerative changes in the intervertebral discs. These discs are the spine's natural shock absorbers: they allow it to move and prevent the nerves being compressed. The disease process is usually accompanied by chronic pain that worsens with physical activity or movement.

Chronic back pain is a symptom of many serious conditions, so it is important to seek qualified medical help at the first sign of trouble. In some cases the most effective treatment may be surgery.

Conservative treatment and physiotherapy can be effective at an early stage, but they usually bring only temporary relief.

Modern medicine has advanced considerably in diagnosing and treating chronic back pain. Developing effective and reliable treatments is a priority for orthopaedic surgeons worldwide. Modern methods are constantly being refined, and traditional approaches are giving way to innovative minimally invasive therapies that speed recovery and are safer for patients.

Intradiscal electrothermal therapy (IDET). The orthopaedics department of the Assuta clinic makes active use of the IDET technique. This is a minimally invasive procedure in which a catheter is introduced into the affected disc and gradually heated to 90°C. The heat causes the structure of the disc to contract and become denser, and destroys the nerve endings that cause the pain.

The operation is carried out under local anaesthetic with light sedation, so that the patient remains conscious and feels no pain.

Preparing for the procedure. Preparation for IDET includes a number of necessary investigations for accurate diagnosis and to study how the condition has developed. CT and MRI of the relevant sections of the spine are used, along with discography with a contrast medium. Biochemistry and clotting tests are also required.

It is important to tell the doctor about any other conditions and allergies, and about any medicines that affect blood clotting. The doctor will give advice on preparing for the operation. Patients are advised not to eat or drink for several hours beforehand.

Recovery. Recovery after IDET is quick and free of discomfort. After the operation the patient stays in a special room for about two hours until the anaesthetic wears off. No long hospital stay is needed, and the patient can go home the same day. Painkillers are needed for the first few weeks. The doctor will give advice on speeding recovery.

The Assuta clinic provides a wide range of medical services to a high standard, as the many positive reports from patients confirm.

fields.title: Meniscus treatment
fields.bodyHtml:
Meniscus treatment in Israel: advanced methods and approaches

Israel holds a leading position worldwide in treating disease and injury of the knee joint, including damage to the meniscus. Thanks to highly qualified specialists, innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment and an individual approach, patients receive effective care and can return to ordinary life quickly.

Diagnosis of meniscal injury

  1. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
    The gold standard in diagnosing meniscal injury, allowing the structure of the knee joint to be assessed in detail.
  2. Ultrasound examination
    Used to assess the soft tissues of the knee and can help identify associated injuries.
  3. X-rays
    Needed to rule out fractures and other bone injuries.
  4. Clinical examination
    Includes specific tests to assess the stability of the joint and identify meniscal damage.

Methods of treating the meniscus in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment
    Includes physiotherapy, orthopaedic supports to stabilise the knee and anti-inflammatory medicines to reduce pain and swelling.
  2. Arthroscopic surgery
    A minimally invasive procedure that allows precise inspection and repair of the damaged meniscus through small incisions, which considerably shortens recovery.
  3. Meniscectomy
    Partial or complete removal of the damaged part of the meniscus. Carried out arthroscopically where the meniscus cannot be repaired.
  4. Meniscal repair
    In some cases the meniscus can be repaired surgically, which preserves its function and prevents degenerative change in the joint.
  5. Meniscal transplantation
    In rare cases, where the meniscus is severely damaged, a donor meniscus may be transplanted.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Advanced medical technology
    Israeli clinics are equipped with the most modern technology, which allows highly precise operations and shortens recovery.
  • Experienced specialists
    Leading orthopaedic and trauma surgeons of international standing with extensive experience in treating meniscal injury.
  • An individual approach
    Treatment in Israel is built on thorough diagnosis and on taking account of every patient's particular circumstances.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation
    Recovery after surgery includes not only physical exercises but individual rehabilitation programmes aimed at an early return to an active life.

Meniscus treatment in Israel gives patients access to highly effective therapies, relieving pain quickly and restoring the function of the knee joint.
